classification.difficultyReason: The same two-Pythagoras structure on a common chord. Here the half-chord must be derived from 12.

content.prompt: Find the exact length of $PQ$, in surd form.

answer.worked:
Let $M$ be the intersection of $PQ$ and $XY$. The line joining the centres bisects the common chord at right angles, so $XM=6\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}PM^2&=PX^2-XM^2\\PM^2&=10^2-6^2=64\\PM&=8\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}QM^2&=QX^2-XM^2\\QM^2&=9^2-6^2=45\\QM&=3\sqrt{5}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}PQ&=PM+QM\\PQ&=(8+3\sqrt{5})\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
